introduction-escaping-yaml-hell.core: Real applications need dozens of near-identical manifests across environments, differing only in a few values. Helm packages manifests as charts with templates and values, renders them per environment, installs them as versioned releases with upgrade and rollback, and shares them through repositories.

first_principles.problem: A team copies 30 YAML files per environment and changes drift between them.

analogy.title: A mail-merge letter template
analogy.story: One template, a list of names and addresses, many personalised letters.
analogy.breaks: Mail-merge has no undo; Helm keeps release history for rollback.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Redis installed with prod values, tracked as a release.

code.text:
helm repo add bitnami https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami
helm install cache bitnami/redis -f values-prod.yaml -n data
helm history cache -n data

check.q: What problem does Helm primarily solve?
check.a: Duplicated, drifting YAML across environments, by templating manifests with values and managing releases.

core-concepts-charts-values-and-releases.core: A chart is a package (Chart.yaml metadata, templates/, values.yaml defaults, optional dependencies). Values are configuration merged from defaults, -f files and --set flags. A release is an installed instance of a chart with a name and namespace; each install or upgrade creates a revision stored as a Secret in the release namespace.

first_principles.problem: Engineers confuse charts, values and releases, and can't tell why a setting was applied.
truths: Packages, config and instances are distinct.

analogy.title: A recipe, your preferences and the dish you served
analogy.story: The recipe is the chart, preferences are values, and each dinner party is a release.
analogy.breaks: Dinners aren't re-served; Helm can roll back to a previous revision exactly.

code.text:
helm get values cache -n data --all
helm get manifest cache -n data | less

check.q: Where does Helm 3 store release history?
check.a: As Secrets in the release's namespace.

how-helm-works-the-templating-engine.core: Helm renders templates with Go templates plus Sprig functions: {{ .Values.x }}, conditionals, range loops, include of named templates from _helpers.tpl, toYaml with nindent for nested blocks, required for mandatory values and lookup for live objects. The rendered YAML is then applied to the cluster.

first_principles.problem: Templates produce invalid YAML because indentation of nested blocks is wrong.
truths: Templates generate text, not structured objects.
derivation: Use **toYaml | nindent N** for nested values.

analogy.title: A mail-merge that must keep exact spacing
analogy.story: Wrong spacing in a form letter is ugly; wrong indentation in YAML breaks it.
analogy.breaks: Letters tolerate formatting errors; Kubernetes rejects invalid YAML.

check.a: Converts a value to YAML and indents it by four spaces on a new line, preserving structure.

artifact-hub-and-chart-repositories.core: Charts are distributed via HTTP chart repositories (index.yaml) or OCI registries (helm push/pull oci://…). Artifact Hub is a discovery site for public charts and other cloud-native packages. Evaluate charts for maintenance, security (images, defaults), provenance (signatures) and values flexibility before using them.

first_principles.problem: A team installs a random public chart that runs privileged containers by default.
truths: Charts are code you run in your cluster.

analogy.title: An app store for cluster software
analogy.story: Read reviews, check the publisher and permissions before installing.
analogy.breaks: App stores vet apps somewhat; chart repos often don't, so you must.

code.text:
helm package ./charts/api
helm push api-1.4.0.tgz oci://123.dkr.ecr.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/charts
helm install api oci://123.dkr.ecr.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/charts/api --version 1.4.0

check.q: What's the modern way to host private Helm charts?
check.a: In an OCI registry (e.g. ECR, GHCR, Harbor).

overriding-values-customizing-a-release.core: Customise releases by layering values files (-f base.yaml -f prod.yaml, later wins), --set for small overrides, --set-file or --set-json for complex input, and subchart values under the dependency name. Use helm diff to preview, --atomic to roll back on failure and --reuse-values carefully (it can hide new defaults).

first_principles.problem: A prod upgrade silently loses a setting because --set flags weren't repeated.
truths: Values merge in a defined order.
Command-line flags are easy to forget.
Upgrades should be previewable and safe.

analogy.title: Layered transparencies of settings
analogy.story: Base settings, then environment overlay, then a tiny sticky note on top.
analogy.breaks: Transparencies are visible; forgotten --set flags vanish on the next upgrade.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Reviewed diff, automatic rollback on failure.

code.text:
helm diff upgrade api ./charts/api -f values.yaml -f values-prod.yaml -n prod
helm upgrade api ./charts/api -f values.yaml -f values-prod.yaml -n prod --atomic --wait --timeout 10m

check.q: When multiple -f files are given, which wins?
check.a: The last file specified overrides earlier ones.

anatomy-of-a-helm-chart-directory.core: A chart directory contains Chart.yaml (name, version, appVersion, dependencies), values.yaml (defaults), values.schema.json (optional validation), templates/ (manifests, _helpers.tpl, NOTES.txt), charts/ (vendored dependencies), crds/ (installed before templates, not upgraded) and templates/tests/ for helm test hooks.

first_principles.problem: A new chart author doesn't know where to put helpers, CRDs or validation.
derivation: Bump **version** for chart changes, **appVersion** for app.

analogy.title: A standard project folder layout
analogy.story: Everyone knows where the README, source and tests live.
analogy.breaks: Project layouts are suggestions; Helm treats crds/ specially (install only, no upgrade).

code.text:
api/
  Chart.yaml
  values.yaml
  values.schema.json
  crds/
  charts/
  templates/
    _helpers.tpl
    deployment.yaml
    service.yaml
    NOTES.txt
    tests/test-connection.yaml

check.q: What's special about CRDs placed in a chart's crds/ directory?
check.a: Helm installs them before templates but never upgrades or deletes them.
